question: Esters are formed by the reaction of:

options.text: alcohol and acid in basic medium
alcohol and aldehyde in the presence of dehydrating agent
alcohol and acid in acidic medium
alcohol and acid at low pressure

solution:
The correct answer is __**alcohol and acid in acidic medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Esterification** is a chemical reaction that results in the formation of at least one **ester**. This typically occurs when a **carboxylic acid** reacts with an **alcohol**.
 
• The reaction requires an **acidic medium** to proceed effectively. This is usually achieved by adding a few drops of a **mineral acid**, most commonly **concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** or **dry hydrogen chloride gas (HCl)**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• In this reaction, the **acid catalyst** serves a vital role by **protonating** the carbonyl oxygen of the carboxylic acid, which increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and facilitates the **nucleophilic attack** by the alcohol molecule.
